Hi Alice — thanks for the details and the CSV, that helps. Short answer first, then a concrete example.

Short answer: Hosted API billing for rerank/classifier scoring is a hybrid of per-request and per-token metering. We have a baseline per-request unit for each scoring call plus per-input token charges for the model work. For rerank: we charge a small per-candidate evaluation unit + the token usage for the model context (query + candidate payload). For classifier: typically a per-instance evaluation unit plus token usage for prompt + example/context tokens.

Concrete example (your 1k-token query + 50 short documents):
- Base call fee: 1 evaluation unit per API call (this covers request overhead and routing).
- Candidate fee: 50 candidate-evaluation units (we price candidates at a lower per-unit than full-generation tokens).
- Token fee: model tokens consumed = tokens(query) + tokens(all candidates after tokenization) + tokens for any system prompt/prefix. We bill per 1k input tokens for scoring work (no separate output token charge for pure rerank where model doesn't return generated text, but we do bill tokens used to compute scores).

So, in practice your invoice line would show: 1 call unit + 50 candidate units + X token units (where X = total input tokens / 1000).

Tiers / SKUs: we expose two main SKUs for scoring workloads on Hosted:
- real_time.rerank (low latency, per-candidate evaluation unit + token charge)
- batch.rerank (optimized for large offline batches, cheaper per-candidate evaluation unit and lower token multiplier)
Similar split exists for classifier. Batch SKUs are cheaper per unit but have longer completion SLOs.

Discounts: we offer volume discounts that apply to candidate-evaluation units and token units separately. For example, at 500k candidate-evaluations/month you get 15% off candidate unit price; token discounts start at 10M token-units/month. Exact thresholds can be negotiated on committed reserved capacity.

Hi Alice — quick follow-up with concrete numbers using the CSV you shared. I mapped your columns to our SKUs and made a couple of assumptions (listed at the bottom). Summary here so procurement can paste into the SOW: 

Estimate (monthly, sample bucket: 50 candidate per query, 1k token query):
- Base call fee: 100k calls -> 100k call-units -> billed at $0.002 per call = $200
- Candidate-evaluation units: 5M candidates -> billed at $0.0006 per candidate = $3,000
- Token units: 600M input tokens (total) -> billed at $1.20 per 1k tokens = $720
- Subtotal hosted scoring = $3,920/month

If you move to batch.rerank for the same volume we can switch candidate-eval to $0.00035 (same token rates) -> subtotal $2,850/month.

Notes & assumptions:
1) Token unit pricing above is for standard float16 models on Hosted. Quantized model options (dedicated/private) can reduce token charge by ~20-40% depending on model.
2) We do not double-bill context tokens for scoring; tokens are only counted once per request.
3) If you require scored output with explanations (generated text), the output tokens are billed separately under generation.token units. The estimate above assumes score-only responses.
4) Reserved capacity commitments (12-month) can convert per-unit pricing into blended committed rates and bring candidate-eval below $0.0004 in many cases.

If this looks in line, I can generate a formal rate-card PDF and a simple contract amendment showing tiered pricing, or we can open a reserved-capacity term sheet.
